Consider the vector $\mathbf{v}$ shown above. Find the vector $A\mathbf{v}$ given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors. Computing the images of $\{ \mathbf{i},\mathbf{j} \}$ under $A,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =Ai=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j \\ {j}^{′} & =Aj=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13991115/assets/414cb72ff004fe4c5898a0e2c7b60b4b3651473e776388fad21efd8fc9ae6165.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $A\mathbf{v},$ we need to rotate $\mathbf{v}$ counterclockwise by an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13991115/assets/b24d8d460b7833a49f2bd7183f0f4b5d22d94a7d3b1d3bb9eb51beff9eeb7ef6.png)

feedback.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(4,4),(-3,-3),(-1,7).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(3,-3)$
- $(-4,-4)$
- $(1,-7)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ is given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{{180}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -3 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 & 1 \\ -4 & 3 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-4,-4),(3,3),(1,-7).$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only."
